title: International Clinical Data Registry for Patients with Rare Embryonal or Sarcomatous CNS Tumors of the German Society for Pediatric Oncology and Hematology (GPOH)
summary: Tumors of the central nervous system (CNS) are the most common solid tumors in childhood and account for a high morbidity and highest mortality of affected patients despite intense multimodal treatment approaches. Highly important for informed treatment decisions in all pediatric CNS tumors is the precise neuropathological and molecular evaluation according to criteria established by the World Health Organization (WHO) (1). Besides the more common malignant embryonal brain tumors in children such as medulloblastoma, a group of tumors was formerly termed supratentorial primitive neuroectodermal tumors, short CNS-PNETs. The development of modern molecular diagnostic tools in recent years made it possible not only to identify these tumors as a very heterogenous group but also to reclassify them by means of DNA methylation analysis (2,3). Formerly known tumor types such as embryonal tumors with multilayered rosettes (ETMR) were more precisely defined and four new types were delineated: CNS neuroblastoma with FOXR2 activation; high-grade neuroepithelial tumor with BCOR internal tandem duplication, Ewing family tumors with CIC alteration and Astroblastoma with MN1 alteration. All of these new tumor types have found their way into the 5th WHO classification of CNS tumors of 2021 (some of them with slightly different designations) and are part of this registry.
conditions: Rare embryonal and sarcomatous brain tumors in children
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of a rare embryonal or sarcomatous CNS tumor confirmed by reference neuropathology for patients age 0-18 years
Signed informed consent by patient and/or caregiver
Exclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of another brain tumor
